## Installation ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/card ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle, } from "@/components/cadence/card"; import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; export function Plan() { return ( Parity plan 57 components, nine batches, one release train.

The width is `w-fit`, so it resolves against the content and still re-wraps when the window narrows. The height comes from a `ResizeObserver` on the content box and is written in the frame the content changed. This is measurement, not motion: no recipe, no duration, nothing to skip under `prefers-reduced-motion` — the box is the same in every mode. ```tsx
Short Two lines, and the card is two lines tall. Stretched This card fills the row, like a normal grid item. …and keeps the extra height it was given.
``` Reach for it when the content is the thing being compared and equal card heights would be a lie — a picker where each option shows its own details, a list where one row has an extra field. Do **not** use it to opt a card out of a layout the rest of the page follows: a grid of cards is usually meant to line up. ## Section boundaries Add a rule with utilities rather than a new part; the `[.border-b]` selectors are already wired: ```tsx … … ``` ## When to use - A unit of content that belongs together: a summary, a plan, an account, a record in a grid. - A surface that needs a header, an optional action, body content, and a footer. - A list of comparable items where the boundary itself carries meaning. ## When not to use - To fake spacing. A card is a boundary; use padding if you only need breathing room. - As a page layout. Nesting cards inside cards flattens the hierarchy. - For a modal or a popover; those are overlays with their own focus rules. ## API | Part | Props | Notes | | ----------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `Card` | `size`, `fit`, native div props | `size` sets `--card-spacing` and `data-size`; `fit`: `"content"` hugs the content. | | `CardHeader` | native div props | Grid header; reacts to `CardAction` and a bottom border. | | `CardTitle` | native div props | Bold, leading-none. Does not create a heading. | | `CardDescription` | native div props | Muted supporting text. | | `CardAction` | native div props | Top-right slot inside the header. | | `CardContent` | native div props | Body; carries the horizontal padding. | | `CardFooter` | native div props | Bottom row; reacts to a top border. | Every part sets `data-slot`, so CSS can reach it: `[&>[data-slot=card-header]]:gap-4`. Under `fit="content"` the parts are wrapped in one `data-slot="card-flow"` box, which is the element the height is measured from — style the parts from the shell as before, and the flow box only if you need the measured layer itself. ## Motion contract No motion (T0). A card does not fade, lift, or scale in. If a group of cards should appear in sequence, that is a page-level `list.stagger` decision made by the parent, not a property of the card. `fit="content"` adds no row to the table below: the measured height is applied as soon as it is known, so there is no phase, no interpolation, and no reduced-motion branch to keep — the geometry is information, and both modes render it identically. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ---------- | ----- | ------------- | | – | none | – | – | | reduced | none | – | – | | none | none | – | – | ## Accessibility - `Card` is a plain `div`: no role, no landmark. That is correct for a visual grouping — but it means the card is not a navigable region. If a set of cards is the main content, wrap it in a `

    `, or render the card with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the title's id. - A card that is clickable must contain a real link or button; do not put `onClick` on the card and call it done — it is invisible to keyboard users. ## Notes for AI - Use `CardFooter` for actions, not a bare `div` — it keeps spacing consistent when `size` changes. - Do not add hover lift to a card that is not interactive. Motion on a static card is decoration (P9). - `fit="content"` is opt-in and per card. A grid of cards is meant to line up; only reach for the content-sized variant when the differences between cards are the information.
